name: chamfered_door_portal
title: a sci-fi doorway with cut corners, an opening 4 studs wide in a wall 2 studs thick.
why: The standard sci-fi doorway, 4 studs wide in a wall 2 thick; an agent reaches for it at every door of a station, ship interior, or corridor.
note: Leaves the opening open (no door part); a sliding door could go in later.

name: hangar_chevron_floor
title: a smooth black hangar deck, fully tiled, with white chevrons down its middle and a framed lift pad.
why: A finished sci-fi deck for hangars and landing bays: fully tiled, with markings that say where ships go and a lift pad.
note: Chevrons are two triangular tiles per 2 x 2 square (marking and deck color) instead of printed tiles. Variant of tiled_floor with markings.

name: recessed_glow_panel
title: a glowing light panel set between two curved lips on a hull wall, all on side studs.
why: Lights a hull or wall face: a glowing panel set between curved lips, all on side studs, for ships, stations, and engine bays.
note: The book frames a curved printed glow panel; this uses plain 2 x 2 tiles in Trans-Light Blue (the 2 x 4 tile was never made in it) and curved slopes 2 x 1 hung vertically as lips. The lower lip needs the 5-plate side-stud brick (22885): a curved slope's thin end is where it takes a side stud.

name: lit_window_panel
title: a sci-fi wall of tall pale-blue light panels between dark pillars, a gray rail along the top.
why: Makes a dark sci-fi room glow: tall pale-blue windows between black pillars, for corridors, throne rooms, and control rooms.

name: checker_light_wall
title: a control wall of red and white light squares in a black frame, a tiled plate stood upright on side studs.
why: A busy control or detention wall in two light colors, a tiled plate stood upright on side studs; a cheap way to fill a sci-fi wall.
note: The lights panel is a submodel built flat and placed with Rot(x=90); the backing's 5-plate side-stud bricks match a plate's stud pitch, so every anti-stud is held.

name: glow_trim_edge
title: a dark platform with a thin lit line all round its edge and indicator lights along its front.
why: A lit line round a platform or dais edge, with indicator lights, for command decks, thrones, and landing pads.
note: Built as a whole platform (three plate courses, the middle one's ring in the glow color) rather than a trim added to an existing edge.

name: pipe_column_cluster
title: a bank of big round pipes or reactor columns of uneven heights, banded and capped, packed side by side.
why: Banks of big pipes or reactor columns that make an engine room, reactor, or industrial corner look busy.
note: Variant of greeble_strip as a column cluster. The book's biggest pipes use curved panels (6059); left out.

name: ribbed_side_panel
title: a big flat wall face cut by deep vertical grooves, built flat and stood on side studs, with girder panels between as framed openings.
why: Big flat walls with depth for platforms, hangars, and station sides: deep vertical grooves, girder bays between.
note: Variant of snot_panel. The book steps its courses with plates and hangs the slab on brackets; this builds the ribs as bricks capped with tiles on a plate and hangs it on 5-plate side-stud bricks.

name: lattice_tower
title: a tall open steel tower of stacked modules, each a deck, corner posts, X-braced girder faces, and a ribbed core.
why: A repeatable tower module for launch towers, cranes, masts, and pylons: deck, corner posts, X-braced faces, ribbed core.
note: The research's grid fallback: X-braced girder panels (64448) for the faces instead of bars in clips at 45 degrees, and plain 8 x 8 decks instead of plate rings. Every module is the same; the book varies the bracing.

name: bar_truss_brace
title: thin diagonal struts from ground anchors up to a tower leg, each a bar with a clip at both ends snapped onto handles, so every brace makes a triangle.
why: Thin diagonal struts that brace a tower leg or frame, for launch towers, cranes, and gantries.
note: Fixed angle by design: two bar holders with clips (11090) and a bar 3L make exactly 100 LDU between handles, and the only grid spacing that matches is 3 studs by 10 plates (a 3-4-5 triangle, about 53 degrees). Struts are placed with add_raw; the validator connects both clips. A plate with one handle (2540) as the ground anchor collides with the clip near the handle's end support, so both anchors are double-handle plates (18649) with the clip at the handle's middle.

name: round_deck_dome
title: a low stepped dome or bridge on top of a disc or hull, round plates of shrinking size stacked on one center.
why: A low stepped dome or bridge on top of a disc, saucer, or hull deck.

name: clamshell_pod
title: a dark round pod with a seat inside, open at the front, whose domed cap lifts on a post to let a figure in.
why: A pod, escape capsule, or meditation chamber a figure sits in, with a cap that lifts.
note: Simplified: the book's petals on hinges are left out (the front stays open), and the cap's lift is two fixed poses: closed on a short post, lifted on a 1 x 2 x 5 brick. The example shows both.

name: plank_deck
title: a wooden deck or floor of long boards with staggered butt joints, laid over plates on cross beams.
why: A wooden deck or floor of staggered boards on beams, for ship decks, piers, cabins, and taverns.
note: Variant of tiled_floor (a planks mode with staggered joints) merged from the MS plank_deck_tiles and FM plank_deck_and_beams entries.

name: davit_lifeboat
title: a small double-ended boat hanging outboard beside a ship's deck from two curved davits.
why: Small boats hanging beside a ship's deck, for steamers, liners, and expedition ships.
note: Grid davits: a post of round bricks, a 1 x 3 plate arm, and a curved slope as the bent head, with the boat pressed onto the arms' undersides. The book bends bars in clips for the davits.

name: round_funnel
title: a tall round ship's funnel or chimney of 4 x 4 round bricks, a dark band at the top, steam pipes up its side.
why: A round ship's funnel or industrial chimney with a dark top and steam pipes.
note: Variant of chimney_stack and exhaust_stack (round, 4 x 4). The book's steam pipes are curved bars; these are round 1 x 1 brick columns.

name: rock_mosaic_panel
title: a sheer cliff face of interlocking wedge facets with tan strata, built flat and hung upright on side studs.
why: A sheer faceted cliff or rock spur face with strata, for fantasy cities, mountains, and cave walls.
note: Variant of rock_facet: a seeded mosaic of wedge plates built flat (a submodel) and hung upright on 5-plate side-stud bricks. The panel's studs face out, as in the book.

name: double_arch_colonnade
title: an open arcade of tall arches on slender round columns, paired where two arches meet, with a cornice line over them.
why: An open arcade of tall arches on slim columns, for cloisters, palaces, and white fantasy cities.
note: Variant of brick_built_arch. Straight runs only; the book's hidden side-stud brick for arches meeting at a corner is left out.

name: fin_merlon_crenels
title: battlements whose merlons are thin rounded fins, not square blocks, with grille tiles in the crenels.
why: Battlements with rounded fin merlons, for fantasy and elven walls where square merlons look too plain.
note: Variant of battlements. The book clips curved slopes onto bars to make each fin; this tops a 1 x 2 brick with two quarter domes (5848) back to back on the grid, so the fins are 2 wide and round to the front.

name: round_bastion
title: a short round pier with a smooth face, for the rounded end of a wall run or a slim tower, 2 studs across.
why: A slim round pier or the rounded end of a wall run, for fantasy walls and small towers too narrow for round_tower.

name: fountain_court
title: a small walled-city courtyard at mini scale, a round fountain at its heart, low hedges, a tapering stone path from the gate, and a white tree.
why: A mini-scale courtyard with fountain, hedges, path, and tree, for walled cities and palace gardens seen from far off.
note: Variant of pond and flagstone_paving at mini scale. The white tree is leaves 4 x 3 (2423) in white on round bricks rather than bars and flower stems (the stems weren't made in white).
